title.narrative: Envelope 3 : GOPA-DERD's response to emergency situation expected across Syria.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe recent armed conflict in As-Sweida Governorate, which started on 13 July 2025 has led to large scale of displacement of families within As-Sweida governorate and from As-Sweida Governorate to Dara’ countryside. The conflict has led to the killing and injuring of thousands of individuals as well as to a large scale of destruction in the As-Sweida city and other villages. The conflict also led to the abduction of hundreds of civilians including women. No available news on many people from the city of As-Sweida city and other villages being considered of unknown destiny. Moreover, the whole Governorate suffers from the lack of basic needs and commodities with the complete loss of water supply, electricity supply, and other main and basic services.ltbrgtThere is a severe lack of food items in As-Sweida Governorate. Bakeries have stopped functioning. There is a severe lack of food items especially due to the blockage of Damascus As-Sweida road. The dependency is on available food items prior to the eruption of the conflict. Water supply infrastructure including water networks and wells was severely damaged to the ongoing conflict. One of the main water sources “Al Thaeleh well) is not functioning along with other wells due to the destruction and the lack of electricity supply.ltbrgtThrough this program's activities, clean water will be provided to affected areas by equipping water wells and connecting them to the public water network. ?Also family hygiene kits will also be distributed to support those affected people to secure basic hygiene. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAlso severe humanitarian crisis grips Daraa following a recent wave of displacement, exacerbating an already dire situation. Displaced families, many living in overcrowded shelters or open areas, face acute food shortages and skyrocketing prices. The collapse of livelihoods and disrupted supply chains have made basic staples unaffordable for most. Reports indicate widespread hunger, with many relying on a single meal a day, often lacking nutritional value. This food insecurity, compounded by a lack of medical care and clean water, has pushed the population to the brink, requiring urgent and unhindered humanitarian aid to prevent a full-scale catastrophe.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThrough this program, food parcels will be distributed to displaced families by distributing 4,032 food parcels over a period of two months.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtltbrgtlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtIntervention in response to the current situation in Aleppo:lt/bgtltbrgtThe current situation for people displaced from Aleppo neighborhoods in early January 2026 is acute and rapidly deteriorating due to intense clashes. Tens of thousands, with estimates ranging from 30,000 by the UN to 155,000 by the Aleppo governor, have fled fighting between government forces and Kurdish-led groups in the Sheikh Maqsoud and Ashrafiyeh neighborhoods. These families, facing severe winter conditions, are sheltering in mosques, collective centers in Aleppo city, or have fled to the Afrin district, overwhelming local capacity. Critical civilian infrastructure has been damaged, including hospitals that have ceased operations, compounding the humanitarian crisis and heightening health risks for vulnerable groups. ltbrgtThe response to this situation in the affected areas will be through the provision of cash assistance of $1,000 for minor repairs to the partly damaged homes of those affected by the recent clashes in the Ashrafieh and Sheikh Maqsoud areas, thereby ensuring a healthy environment, a decent life, and reducing protection risks for the affected families.ltbrgtlt/pgt
